items.name: Sinus tachycardia
action: A response: find and treat the cause (pain, fever, hypovolemia, hypoxia)
Don't try to slow it down
hints: Count the rate, then look for an upright P wave in front of every QRS, even if it's close to the T wave.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 108/min; rhythm regular; PR 0.16 s, constant; QRS narrow (0.09 s).
Every beat is a normal sinus beat with an upright P wave; only the rate is high, and still under 150.

items.name: Normal sinus rhythm
action: Normal rhythm: assess the patient, not just the monitor
Vitals, glucose, history
hints: Go step by step: rate, regularity, a P before every QRS, the PR interval, then QRS width. Is anything outside normal limits?
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 77/min; rhythm regular; PR 0.16 s, constant; QRS narrow (0.07 s).
Everything is normal. Look for the problem in the patient, not the strip.

items.name: Sinus arrhythmia
rows: Irregular in a smooth cycle (R–R varies by ≥ 0.16 s)
Upright and identical, one before each QRS
action: Normal variant, especially in young people
No treatment
hints: Measure several R–R intervals in a row. Do they change, and if so, gradually or suddenly?
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 80/min (6-second count); rhythm irregular in a smooth cycle (R–R varies by ≥ 0.16 s); PR 0.16 s, constant; QRS narrow (0.08 s).
The P waves never change. Only the spacing changes, gradually.

items.name: Sinoatrial (SA) exit block
action: The pause (1.36 s) is exactly two P–P intervals (0.68 s each)
Monitor; treat as bradycardia if symptomatic
hints: Find the gap and use calipers (or paper) to march the P waves through it.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate ≈ 80/min (6-second count); underlying 88/min; rhythm regular, with one dropped P–QRS–T; PR 0.19 s, constant; QRS narrow (0.08 s).
March out the P waves: the missing beat lands exactly where one was due.

items.name: Sinus bradycardia
action: Asymptomatic: no treatment
Symptomatic: atropine 1 mg IV; pacing or infusion if it fails
hints: Count the rate first, then check that every beat still looks like a normal sinus beat.
Here's what I measure on this one: rate 42/min; rhythm regular; PR 0.13 s, constant; QRS narrow (0.07 s).
Every beat is a normal sinus beat. Only the rate is slow.
